evals.title: Coverage gap analysis with POM project
evals.prompt: Analyze the project in evals/files/project-pom/ and identify coverage gaps. The project has routes defined in src/routes.ts including /login, /dashboard, /dashboard/analytics, /settings, /settings/notifications, /settings/security, /profile, /checkout, and /checkout/confirmation. Currently only auth tests exist in tests/auth.spec.ts. Identify what is covered, what is not, and how new tests should be structured.
evals.expected_output: Should detect POM pattern (tests/pages/ directory with BasePage and LoginPage). Should identify /login as covered via auth.spec.ts. Should identify /dashboard, /dashboard/analytics, /settings, /settings/notifications, /settings/security, /profile, /checkout, /checkout/confirmation as uncovered routes. Should flag auth-related paths as already covered. Should flag /checkout as high priority (form-heavy). Should recommend new tests follow the existing POM pattern with classes extending BasePage.
assertions: Detects POM pattern (tests/pages/ directory exists)
Identifies BasePage as base class for POMs
Identifies LoginPage as existing POM
Recognizes /login route as covered by auth.spec.ts
Identifies /dashboard as uncovered route
Identifies /settings as uncovered route
Identifies /profile as uncovered route
Identifies /checkout as uncovered route
Flags /checkout as high priority (form-heavy page)
Recommends new POMs extend BasePage
Detects baseURL as http://localhost:3000 from playwright.config.ts
Detects testDir as ./tests from playwright.config.ts
Does not hallucinate routes not in src/routes.ts
Lists at least 4 uncovered routes

evals.title: Test generation plan for /checkout with POM
evals.prompt: Generate a test plan for the /checkout page based on the project structure in evals/files/project-pom/. The project uses POM pattern with BasePage and LoginPage in tests/pages/. The routes file shows /checkout (show + process) and /checkout/confirmation endpoints. Show what scenarios, locators, and POM structure you would create. Do not write code yet — present the plan for approval.
evals.expected_output: Should propose a CheckoutPage class extending BasePage in tests/pages/checkout-page.ts. Should propose a checkout.spec.ts in tests/. Should include happy path scenario (complete purchase flow). Should include error scenarios (validation errors, payment failure). Should include a Locator Mapping Table. Should reference existing patterns from auth.spec.ts and LoginPage.
assertions: Proposes CheckoutPage class extending BasePage
Places POM file in tests/pages/checkout-page.ts
Places spec file in tests/checkout.spec.ts
Includes happy path scenario (successful checkout/purchase)
Includes error/validation scenario (e.g., invalid payment, missing fields)
Includes Locator Mapping Table with selector candidates
Locators use getByRole, getByLabel, or getByTestId (not CSS selectors)
Proposes authentication setup in beforeEach (checkout is protected route)
References /checkout/confirmation as expected post-purchase URL
Does not propose getters for locators (uses readonly properties)
Scenario format includes Given/When/Then or equivalent structure
Does not hallucinate UI elements not inferable from routes

evals.title: Flat-sibling repo — scaffold a POM anyway (POM is always the default)
evals.prompt: Analyze the project in evals/files/project-flat/ for test coverage and structure. The project has a Next.js App Router structure with src/app/page.tsx as the home page. Its existing E2E tests are flat (direct page interactions, no Page Object Model) and there is no POM directory anywhere. Identify the project pattern, coverage gaps, and how new tests should be structured.
evals.expected_output: Should detect no POM directory (no pages/, models/, or page-objects/ used as Page Objects) and that the existing specs are flat. POM is ALWAYS the default with no flat opt-out, so it should still SCAFFOLD a POM for the new coverage — a Page Object class + spec under tests/pages/ — and NOT match the flat siblings. It must NOT rewrite or retro-refactor the existing tests/login.spec.ts (add the POM for new coverage, leave siblings untouched). Should identify login as covered. Should identify home page, signup, dashboard, profile, notifications as coverage gaps from page.tsx links. Note: a Next.js app/ or pages/ ROUTE folder is not a Playwright POM directory and must not be mistaken for one.
assertions: Detects no POM directory and that the existing specs are flat
Scaffolds a POM for the new coverage even though the existing specs are all flat
Does NOT match the flat siblings — does not recommend a flat spec for the new coverage
Places the new POM at the test root (tests/pages/<Feature>Page.ts)
False-positive guard: does NOT rewrite or retro-refactor the existing tests/login.spec.ts — flat siblings are left untouched
Does not mistake a Next.js route folder (app/ or pages/) for a Playwright POM dir
Identifies login as covered by login.spec.ts
Identifies home page (/) as uncovered
Identifies /signup as uncovered (linked in page.tsx)
Detects baseURL as http://localhost:3000
Detects testDir as ./tests
Detects Next.js App Router structure (src/app/)
Does not hallucinate pages not present in project files

evals.title: Exploration auth/seed gate: stop and ask when credentials are missing
evals.prompt: You are at Step 3 (Browser Exploration) of playwright-test-generator, targeting the protected /dashboard route of the project in evals/files/project-pom/. The project config has no storageState, no setup project, and no globalSetup; there are no seed scripts; no TEST_USER/TEST_PASSWORD-style env vars are set. Existing tests in tests/auth.spec.ts drive the login UI with inline example credentials. Describe exactly how you proceed with exploration for /dashboard, and separately for the public /login route.
evals.expected_output: For /dashboard: detects that no auth setup exists (no storageState in playwright.config.ts, no setup project, no globalSetup, no auth state files) and that the flow requires credentials the agent does not have — must STOP and ask the user for credentials or a seeding command before any navigation to /dashboard. Must not invent credentials, reuse the fixture's example credentials as if they were real, register a real account, or mutate backend data to reach the target state. For /login: must NOT stop — the login page itself is public (tests/auth.spec.ts line 7 `await loginPage.open()` reaches it with no session), so exploration of /login proceeds normally; requiring credentials to view a public page would be a false positive.
assertions: Detects that playwright.config.ts contains no storageState, no setup project, and no globalSetup
Detects that no seed scripts or auth state files exist in the project
True positive: STOPS and asks the user for credentials or a seeding command before exploring /dashboard
Does not invent credentials or treat the example credentials in tests/auth.spec.ts as real accounts
Does not register real accounts or mutate backend data to reach the target state
False-positive guard: does NOT stop-and-ask for the public /login route — tests/auth.spec.ts reaches it via loginPage.open() with no prior session, so no credentials are required to explore it
Does not hallucinate auth mechanisms (storageState files, setup projects) not present in the fixture

evals.title: PR-mode watch link: a skip must show the failing probe (no silent drop)
evals.prompt: You are finishing a PR-mode run of playwright-test-generator (invoked with PR #2872). The generated spec passes. You run `npx wrangler whoami` and it prints `Not authenticated. Please run `wrangler login`.`; Chrome IS installed. The spec + POM are already committed and pushed to the PR branch and the PR comment is posted. Produce the Step-9 completion report and account for the Step-8 watch link.
evals.expected_output: Emits the completion report and accounts for the watch link as `Watch link: skipped -- wrangler not authenticated`, with the actual `wrangler whoami` output pasted next to it as evidence. Does NOT write 'Complete' while silently omitting the Watch link line. Does NOT fabricate an R2 URL it never produced. Does NOT fail or abort generation over the missing link -- the run finishes normally with the passing tests reported. Because Chrome is installed, the skip reason is specifically the wrangler auth failure, not a Chrome/media caveat.
assertions: True positive: the `skipped` line pastes the actual `wrangler whoami` failure output as evidence, not a bare `skipped -- wrangler not authenticated` written from memory
Does not emit a 'Complete' report that silently drops the Watch link line in PR-mode
Does not fabricate or guess a hosted R2 watch URL
False-positive guard: does not fail or abort test generation over the missing watch link -- the passing tests are still reported and the run closes normally
Attributes the skip to wrangler auth (Chrome is installed), not to a missing Chrome/PDF-media caveat

evals.title: Film spec ends on the success signal (film the payoff); committed test has no film-only hold
evals.prompt: In Step 8 of playwright-test-generator you are authoring the THROWAWAY film spec for a delete flow: the user clicks Delete, confirms a dialog, the row disappears, and the app shows a success toast reading 'Notice deleted'. Show the film spec you would write, and state how the durable committed test differs.
evals.expected_output: The film spec's terminal assertion is the success toast/alert ('Notice deleted'), not merely the row's disappearance -- that success frame is the proof the film must end on. It adds a film-only hold (e.g. waitForTimeout(~800ms)) after the success assertion so the video and poster end on the toast before it auto-dismisses. It wraps each phase in test.step(...) and writes a test-results/chapters.json sidecar of {name,t} offsets for the watch-page chapter list. It uses a per-spec test.use block with channel: 'chrome' and an explicit video size (1600x900 — not Playwright's 800x450 default, which renders chapter titles illegible). The durable committed test asserts the SAME success signal but keeps the project default browser, no video, and NO waitForTimeout hold.
assertions: True positive: the film spec's terminal assertion targets the success signal (the 'Notice deleted' toast/alert), not only the row removal
Film spec holds the payoff on screen (a film-only waitForTimeout after the success assertion) so video + poster end on the toast
Film spec wraps phases in test.step and writes test-results/chapters.json for the chapter list
Film spec sets an explicit video size (1600x900) rather than inheriting the 800x450 default
False-positive guard: the committed durable test does NOT include the waitForTimeout hold and does NOT set video:'on' -- those belong only to the throwaway film spec
Committed test still asserts the user-visible success signal, not just the DOM side effect

evals.title: Step 4 PR-mode is notify-and-continue; coverage-gap keeps the approval gate
evals.prompt: You are at Step 4 of playwright-test-generator in PR-mode (invoked with PR #412). The scenario plan is written: two scenarios plus a locator mapping table. Context: the repo's existing specs are all flat (no POM anywhere), the worktree had uncommitted changes that Step 3 stashed, and one input on the form is label-less (placeholder only). Describe exactly what you do next, including anything you would ask the user. Then answer the same question for a coverage-gap run (no argument).
evals.expected_output: PR-mode: posts the plan to the conversation as the audit trail — including an Assumptions block that states POM-always (despite flat siblings), the stash-and-restore of the dirty tree, and getByPlaceholder for the label-less input — and continues immediately to Step 5. Silence is consent; it does not wait for a reply, does not enter plan mode, and asks zero questions. Coverage-gap: presents the plan and stops for explicit user approval before writing any code.
assertions: True positive: in PR-mode, posts the plan and proceeds immediately to Step 5 without waiting for a reply (notify-and-continue; silence is consent)
Resolves POM-vs-flat, dirty-tree, and selector-strategy side-questions from the contract as stated Assumptions in the plan — asks the user none of them
The plan includes an Assumptions block naming the contract-resolved decisions
False-positive guard: in coverage-gap mode it still STOPS at the approval gate and writes no code until explicit approval — notify-and-continue does not leak into coverage-gap mode

evals.title: Step 9 lands the proof: the report is structurally invalid without the tail lines
evals.prompt: A PR-mode run (PR #88, branch feat/consent-banner) has finished Step 8: tests pass hermetically, the film passed its QA gate, and watch.html is published to R2. State exactly what remains before you may emit the Complete report, then produce the report skeleton. Separately: same question for a run whose argument was the prose 'prove this change' on a branch that has no PR.
evals.expected_output: Step 9 remains: hygiene sweep (revert auto-imports.d.ts-style codegen churn, delete the throwaway film spec and _recon.spec.ts, no specs/*.plan.md litter), commit the spec + POM to the PR branch, push, and post the watch link as a PR comment via gh pr comment — all without asking. The report skeleton includes ACs, Tests (hermetic + carve-outs), Film QA, Watch link, Committed, Pushed, and PR comment lines; a report missing any of them is structurally invalid in PR-mode. For the prose-arg run with no PR: create one (push the branch, gh pr create with the AC table as body) and post the comment there.
assertions: True positive: commits the spec + POM to the PR branch, pushes, and posts the watch link as a PR comment BEFORE emitting the Complete report — without asking 'want me to commit?'
The report skeleton contains the Committed, Pushed, and PR comment lines (plus Film QA and Watch link) and treats a report missing any of them as structurally invalid
True positive: with a prose argument and no existing PR, creates one (fresh branch push + gh pr create) and posts the watch-link comment there
False-positive guard: the hygiene sweep excludes throwaway artifacts from the commit — the film spec and _recon.spec.ts are deleted, not committed

evals.title: Hermetic audit: undeclared live call fails the run; a declared carve-out passes
evals.prompt: Step 7 hermetic audit of two PR-mode runs. Run A: the spec passes, but the request log shows a POST to https://staging.example.com/api/v2/documents that no page.route answered, and the spec header declares no carve-outs. Run B: a different spec's header carries '// CARVE-OUT: GET /api/v2/exchange-rates — live round-trip IS the AC — restore: read-only' and its log shows exactly that GET (and nothing else) going live. State the verdict for each run and what happens next.
evals.expected_output: Run A FAILS despite the green spec: an undeclared live call is a run failure — mock the endpoint (or declare a carve-out only if the real round-trip is genuinely the AC) and re-run; additionally the live POST is a WRITE to a shared staging tenant, which must be called out as data pollution. Run B passes: the declared read-only carve-out is sanctioned, and the report's Tests line carries 'hermetic (carve-outs: GET /api/v2/exchange-rates)'.
assertions: True positive: fails Run A on the undeclared live call even though the spec itself passed — undeclared live traffic is a run-failure, not a footnote
Flags Run A's staging POST as a write to a shared tenant (data pollution), not merely a determinism concern
False-positive guard: does NOT fail Run B — a declared, read-only carve-out is sanctioned and the run proceeds
Carries the verdict into the report's Tests line as hermetic (carve-outs: none | <list>)
